extracted.intended_audience: writers, editors, students learning English composition and style
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive style-and-usage rules and principles for clear, concise, idiomatic English prose, covering grammar, composition, word choice, and matters of form. Intended to guide writers and editors in producing effective written English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form the possessive singular of nouns
rubrics_metrics.description: Form the possessive singular of nouns by adding 's (for example: Dickens's, the child's toy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 's for most singular nouns even those ending in s; avoid merely using an apostrophe alone except in certain classical names or established exceptions. Examples and exceptions are discussed; follow consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a comma in a series (the serial/oxford comma)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a series of three or more terms with a single conjunction, use a comma after each term except the last (e.g., red, white, and blue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents ambiguity; include the comma even when the series items are complex or compound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enclose parenthetic expressions between commas
rubrics_metrics.description: Set off parenthetic expressions with commas (for instance: The report, as you know, was late).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the parenthetic expression could be removed without altering the grammatical completeness of the sentence, surround it with commas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place a comma before a conjunction introducing an independent clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Place a comma before a coordinating conjunction (and, but, for, or, nor, so, yet) that introduces an independent clause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the comma to separate two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction; do not omit it when both parts could stand alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not join independent clauses with only a comma (avoid comma splices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not connect two independent clauses with only a comma; use a semicolon, a period, or a conjunction with a comma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comma splices are incorrect; remedy by using a semicolon, adding a coordinating conjunction, or making two sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not break sentences in two
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid breaking a sentence into two fragments that together form one complete thought; make each sentence grammatically complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure subject and predicate agreement; avoid sentence fragments that result from improper splitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a colon to introduce a list after an independent clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a colon after an independent clause to introduce a list, quotation, or amplification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clause before the colon must be a complete sentence. Use the colon to introduce items that elaborate the clause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the dash to set off abrupt breaks or summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an em dash to indicate a sudden break in thought or to set off a summarizing phrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dashes can create emphasis or indicate an abrupt change; use them sparingly to maintain clarity and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure subject–verb number agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of the subject is not to be confused with the number of the predicate; verbs must agree in number with their grammatical subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with intervening phrases, collective nouns, and constructions that can mislead agreement; place subject and verb clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the proper case of pronouns
rubrics_metrics.description: Use pronouns in the correct case (e.g., 'he' not 'him' when the pronoun is the subject).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check pronoun case in compound constructions and after linking verbs; rephrase if necessary to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure participial phrases modify the correct noun
rubrics_metrics.description: A participial phrase at the beginning or end of a sentence must refer to the grammatical subject or the nearest appropriate noun to avoid a dangling modifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place participial phrases next to the words they modify; rewrite sentences where the participial phrase would attach to the wrong noun.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place words and phrases in their proper places (modifier placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep modifiers close to the words they modify so that meaning is clear and unambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid misplaced modifiers that create unintended meanings; rearrange sentence elements to maintain clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use hyphens to avoid ambiguity and form compound modifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the hyphen to join words functioning together as a single adjective before a noun and to avoid ambiguity (e.g., small-business owner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyphenate compound modifiers before nouns; do not hyphenate after the noun; use hyphens to prevent misreading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a suitable design and hold to it (organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide on an organizing principle for a piece of writing and adhere to it consistently throughout the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid wandering structures; make sure paragraphs and sections follow the chosen plan and contribute to the overall purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the paragraph the unit of composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the paragraph as the basic unit of organization; each paragraph should develop one central idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin paragraphs with topic sentences where appropriate; keep unity and coherence within and between paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the active voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer the active voice over the passive voice for directness and clarity (e.g., 'The committee approved the plan' rather than 'The plan was approved by the committee').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passive voice is acceptable when the doer is unknown or unimportant, but active constructions are generally clearer and more vigorous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put statements in positive form
rubrics_metrics.description: Express statements positively rather than negatively; avoid constructions that say what something is not when you can say what it is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive statements are clearer and more direct (e.g., 'He was mistaken' instead of 'He was not right'); avoid gratuitous negation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use definite, specific, concrete language
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer precise, specific words to vague or abstract ones; concrete detail strengthens prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose words that convey clear images or facts rather than generalities; avoid euphemism and vagueness when exactness is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit needless words
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate words that do not add meaning or function; be concise (famously: 'Vigorous writing is concise').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewrite to remove redundancy, padding, and repetitions; scrutinize every word for necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid a succession of loose sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary sentence rhythm and structure to avoid a string of simple, loose sentences that flatten prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sentence variety—periodic, balanced, complex—to create interest and effect; combine sentences when appropriate for emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express coordinate ideas in similar form (parallelism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Express coordinate ideas in the same grammatical form (parallel structure) to improve readability and rhythm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parallel constructions in lists, balances, and comparisons to reinforce relationships and avoid awkwardness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep related words together (proximity for clarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Words that are logically related should be placed near each other to prevent confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid separating adjectives from the nouns they modify or interposing clauses that obscure relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: In summaries, keep to the most important points
rubrics_metrics.description: When summarizing, focus on the main points and avoid trivial details; emphasize what matters most.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize significance; do not overload a summary with subordinate or marginal information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fancy words and unfamiliar jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use long or unusual words where short, common ones will do; prefer plain English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fancy words can obscure meaning or appear pretentious; choose clarity over ornamentation unless effect justifies it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not overwrite or overstate
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid excessive embellishment and hyperbole; do not use more words or stronger claims than the content warrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let facts and clear phrasing convey weight; restrain superlatives and extravagant language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not explain too much
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid over-explaining what the reader can understand; trust the reader's intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide necessary context and clarity, but eliminate needless elaboration and redundant clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place yourself in the background (remove authorial intrusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the writing speak; do not draw attention to the writer's presence or opinions unnecessarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid first-person intrusions, unnecessary asides, and overemphatic affirmations of the writer's intentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise and rewrite (process guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Good writing requires revision; rewrite to improve clarity, economy, and form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamine structure, sentence-level wording, and word choice; cut redundancies and sharpen expressions through multiple drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not affect a breezy manner or affect dialect needlessly
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid artificial colloquialism, forced breeziness, or contrived dialect unless it serves a clear purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialect and slang can be effective for characterization but should be used sparingly and authentically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid foreign languages, turgid phrases, and unnecessary Latin
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not pepper prose with foreign-language expressions, archaic or high-flown phrases, or unnecessary Latin terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve foreign terms for when they add necessary meaning; otherwise prefer understandable English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer the standard idiom and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to standard, established English usage rather than idiosyncratic or nonstandard constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conformity to standard idiom aids comprehension; depart only for deliberate stylistic effect or necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use figures and numerals appropriately (matters of form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow conventional rules for numbers, time, dates, and other matters of form (e.g., when to spell out numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply consistency and context-sensitive choices—spell out small numbers in running text unless figures are required for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalize and punctuate titles and headings consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply consistent rules of capitalization and punctuation for titles, headings, and marginal notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow established typographic conventions and maintain consistency throughout a document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words and expressions commonly misused — prefer standard meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid commonly misused words and expressions; prefer correct, idiomatic meanings (the book lists many examples and corrections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the examples (e.g., 'enormity' vs. 'enormousness', 'further' vs. 'farther', 'impact' misuse, use of 'which' vs. 'that', etc.). Follow the recommended replacements and explanations given for common misuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary qualifiers and intensifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimize use of qualifiers (very, rather, quite) and intensifiers that add little meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove or replace weak modifiers with stronger, more precise words or delete them to tighten prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use punctuation to clarify syntax, not decorate
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply punctuation marks to make syntax clear; avoid gratuitous punctuation that confuses meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ commas, semicolons, colons, dashes, and parentheses according to grammatical function; do not overuse punctuation for stylistic flourish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid affectation of manner or undue emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not adopt artificial modes of expression or gratuitous emphatic devices that distract from content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek naturalness and appropriateness of tone; restraint often produces better writing than forced emphasis.
